turns.q:
Your response was: "I mean... I looked through it. There were some parts that felt familiar, some that didn't quite. I'm not sure I'm the right person to say whether it all makes sense — it depends a lot on who would normally use this. I suppose some things stuck with me a bit more than others — there was a section with numbers, prices I think, and it took me longer than I expected to find the main one. Something about the way the numbers were presented didn't quite add up for me. I couldn't say much more than that without thinking about it more."

We want to understand what you meant by "something about the way the numbers were presented didn't quite add up for me", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The visual hierarchy of the prices, specifically how the individual item price ($39.99) is displayed in a much larger font than the final Total ($288.99).
B) The alignment of the text and numbers within the Order Summary box, where the labels are left-aligned but the prices are right-aligned.
C) The grouping of the calculation details (Subtotal, Shipping, Total) at the bottom of the summary section rather than being integrated with the item list.
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
turns.a: If I had to pick... probably A? The sizes not forming a clear hierarchy, or not being able to spot the total without reading through everything. I think. Though I'm not sure that's exactly it.

turns.q: Looking at the Order Summary, how does the visual weight of the $39.99 price compare to the Total amount in terms of what you expect to pay?
turns.a: There was just... a lot of numbers happening. I'm not sure what I was focusing on. Some of them seemed more prominent than others but not in a way I could explain. It was more of an overall impression — I couldn't quickly tell which number was the most important one.

turns.q: If a developer built this layout exactly as shown, how would that ambiguity impact someone trying to confirm their final cost before proceeding?
turns.a: It's just a general impression, really. Nothing I can point to exactly. There were numbers of different sizes but I couldn't tell you which ones I was supposed to be focusing on — it's like that.

turns.q: If the layout clearly highlighted the total as the most important number, would that resolve your concern, or is there something else about how these prices are arranged that still feels off?
turns.a: There were — I think several different text sizes in that price section? Some of the numbers were bigger than others. But the bigger ones weren't necessarily the ones I needed most. The total — I think it was the total — was in a certain size, but then there were other numbers that seemed almost as large. And then some that were quite small. None of them felt like they were arranged with any particular intention. I couldn't tell what the hierarchy was supposed to be.

turns.q: If the design team could only change one structural thing about how those prices are sized and placed, what specific adjustment would make the total unmistakably clear?
turns.a: I'll be honest — I nearly just moved on without confirming the total, because I couldn't immediately spot which number it was. I kept looking for the one that should be obviously the total and none of them were. So I stopped and read the labels one by one to make sure I had the right number before moving forward.

turns.q: If the design team could only change one structural thing about how those prices are sized and placed, what specific adjustment would make the total unmistakably clear?
turns.a: What I meant was... the numbers should have a clearer relationship to each other in terms of size. The total should obviously be the most prominent — clearly larger than the rest. And the smaller details — the breakdown items, the labels — should all be clearly smaller. Right now it feels like there are too many different sizes and none of them explain themselves. If the total stood out immediately as the most important number, I'd have found it without reading anything around it.
